chapter: The war years: Barnet, Hot Lips Page, Newton and Kirby
title: The Palmer Brothers trio, 1931-32
summary: Early in the Thirties he played with the Palmer Brothers and Kirby, who sang in harmony; they discuss Clarence Palmer's scat.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: When were you with the Palmer Brothers?
This is ancient. That was '31, '32... That would be in between there. It didn't happen, but we tried to make it. We played a few hotel dates and... But it didn't come off.
Just you, Kirby and the drummer with the Palmer Brothers?
That was in the early Thirties.
They were the first ones to sing in harmony. Do you remember them?
Yeah, I remember them. There was a good one, too, who... Clarence was a good singer.
There was Clarence, Ernie and Vic.
Clarence could have made it as a solo. He was excellent.
Whew! He was a terrific scatter. He reminded me of Leo Watson.

Yeah, but he had a hit, too. He sang a song called 'Brown...' -- brown something. But he really made a hit. Of course, he played the (?) with Earl Hines in Chicago and all sorts of... And then, of course, they worked with Cab
